## Diagnosis

**File:** `AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/Previewer.java`

The `Previewer` activity declares only `android:configChanges="locale"` in the manifest, so a screen rotation **destroys and recreates** the activity (unlike `Reviewer`, which declares `orientation|screenSize` and handles rotation itself).

On recreation, `Previewer.onCreate()` re-read its entire state from the launching `Intent`:

```java
mCardList = getIntent().getLongArrayExtra("cardList");
mIndex = getIntent().getIntExtra("index", -1);
```

The `Intent` is immutable and still holds the *original* starting index from `CardBrowser`. Every navigation the user performed (`mIndex++` / `mIndex--` in `mSelectScrollHandler`) lived only in the in-memory field and was never persisted — `Previewer` overrode neither `onSaveInstanceState` nor `onRestoreInstanceState`. So rotation discarded all navigation and snapped the preview back to the card the browser originally opened.

The same applied to `mShowingAnswer`: `onCollectionLoaded()` unconditionally called `displayCardQuestion()`, so rotating while viewing an answer also flipped back to the question side.

## Fix

1. **Added `onSaveInstanceState()`** persisting `mIndex` and `mShowingAnswer`.
2. **`onCreate()` prefers the saved bundle over the Intent** when `savedInstanceState != null`, falling back to the Intent values as defaults (so a fresh launch is unchanged).
3. **`onCollectionLoaded()` restores the visible side** — it still calls `displayCardQuestion()` first (required, since that's what populates `mTypeCorrect`/`mTypeInput` and the sound list that `displayCardAnswer()` consumes), then replays `displayCardAnswer()` if the answer was showing. Capturing `restoreAnswer` into a local is necessary because `displayCardQuestion()` clears `mShowingAnswer`.
4. **Hardened the guard** with a `mCardList == null` check — previously that line would NPE if the extra were ever absent.

Since `updateButtonState()` reads `mIndex`/`mShowingAnswer`, the `<`/`>` navigation buttons and their disabled-at-the-edges states also come back correct after rotation.

601	    private void updateTypeAnswerInfo() {
602	        mTypeCorrect = null;
603	        mTypeInput = "";
604	        String q = mCurrentCard.q(false);
605	        Matcher m = sTypeAnsPat.matcher(q);
606	        int clozeIdx = 0;
607	        if (!m.find()) {
608	            return;
609	        }
610	        String fld = m.group(1);
611	        // if it's a cloze, extract data
612	        if (fld.startsWith("cloze:", 0)) {
613	            // get field and cloze position
614	            clozeIdx = mCurrentCard.getOrd() + 1;
615	            fld = fld.split(":")[1];
616	        }
617	        // loop through fields for a match
618	        try {
619	            JSONArray ja = mCurrentCard.model().getJSONArray("flds");
620	            for (int i = 0; i < ja.length(); i++) {
621	                String name = (String) (ja.getJSONObject(i).get("name"));
622	                if (name.equals(fld)) {
623	                    mTypeCorrect = mCurrentCard.note().getItem(name);
624	                    if (clozeIdx != 0) {
625	                        // narrow to cloze
626	                        mTypeCorrect = contentForCloze(mTypeCorrect, clozeIdx);
627	                    }
628	                    mTypeFont = (String) (ja.getJSONObject(i).get("font"));
629	                    mTypeSize = (int) (ja.getJSONObject(i).get("size"));
630	                    break;
631	                }
632	            }
633	        } catch (JSONException e) {
634	            throw new RuntimeException(e);
635	        }
636	        if (mTypeCorrect == null) {
637	            if (clozeIdx != 0) {
638	                mTypeWarning = getResources().getString(R.string.empty_card_warning);
639	            } else {
640	                mTypeWarning = getResources().getString(R.string.unknown_type_field_warning, fld);
641	            }
642	        } else if ("".equals(mTypeCorrect)) {
643	            mTypeCorrect = null;
644	        } else {
645	            mTypeWarning = null;
646	        }
647	    }

657	    private String typeAnsQuestionFilter(String buf) {
658	        Matcher m = sTypeAnsPat.matcher(buf);
659	        if (mTypeWarning != null) {

661	        }

663	        if (mUseInputTag) {
664	            // These functions are defined in the JavaScript file assets/scripts/card.js. We get the text back in
665	            // shouldOverrideUrlLoading() in createWebView() in this file.
666	            sb.append("<center>\n<input type=text name=typed id=typeans onfocus=\"taFocus();\" " +
667	                      "onblur=\"taBlur(this);\" onKeyPress=\"return taKey(this, event)\" autocomplete=\"off\" ");
668	            // We have to watch out. For the preview we don’t know the font or font size. Skip those there. (Anki
669	            // desktop just doesn’t show the input tag there. Do it with standard values here instead.)
670	            if (mTypeFont != null && !TextUtils.isEmpty(mTypeFont) && mTypeSize > 0) {
671	                sb.append("style=\"font-family: '").append(mTypeFont).append("'; font-size: ")
672	                        .append(Integer.toString(mTypeSize)).append("px;\" ");
673	            }
674	            sb.append(">\n</center>\n");
675	        } else {
676	            sb.append("<span id=typeans class=\"typePrompt");
677	            if (mUseInputTag) {
678	                sb.append(" typeOff");
679	            }
680	            sb.append("\">........</span>");
681	        }
682	        return m.replaceAll(sb.toString());

686	    /**
687	     * Fill the placeholder for the type comparison. Show the correct answer, and the comparison if appropriate.
688	     *
689	     * @param buf The answer text
690	     * @param userAnswer Text typed by the user, or empty.
691	     * @param correctAnswer The correct answer, taken from the note.
692	     * @return The formatted answer text
693	     */
694	    private String typeAnsAnswerFilter(String buf, String userAnswer, String correctAnswer) {
695	        Matcher m = sTypeAnsPat.matcher(buf);
696	        DiffEngine diffEngine = new DiffEngine();
697	        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
698	        sb.append("<div");
699	        sb.append("><code id=typeans>");
700	
701	        // We have to use Matcher.quoteReplacement because the inputs here might have $ or \.
702	
703	        if (!TextUtils.isEmpty(userAnswer)) {
704	            // The user did type something.
705	            if (userAnswer.equals(correctAnswer)) {
706	                // and it was right.
707	                sb.append(Matcher.quoteReplacement(DiffEngine.wrapGood(correctAnswer)));
708	                sb.append("\u2714"); // Heavy check mark
709	            } else {
710	                // Answer not correct.
711	                // Only use the complex diff code when needed, that is when we have some typed text that is not
712	                // exactly the same as the correct text.
713	                String[] diffedStrings = diffEngine.diffedHtmlStrings(correctAnswer, userAnswer);
714	                // We know we get back two strings.
715	                sb.append(Matcher.quoteReplacement(diffedStrings[0]));
716	                sb.append("<br>↓<br>");
717	                sb.append(Matcher.quoteReplacement(diffedStrings[1]));
718	            }
719	        } else {
720	            if (!mUseInputTag) {
721	                sb.append(Matcher.quoteReplacement(DiffEngine.wrapMissing(correctAnswer)));
722	            } else {
723	                sb.append(Matcher.quoteReplacement(correctAnswer));
724	            }
725	        }
726	        sb.append("</code></div>");
727	        return m.replaceAll(sb.toString());
728	    }

731	    /**
732	     * Return the correct answer to use for {{type::cloze::NN}} fields.
733	     *
734	     * @param txt The field text with the clozes
735	     * @param idx The index of the cloze to use
736	     * @return A string with a comma-separeted list of unique cloze strings with the corret index.
737	     */
738	
739	    private String contentForCloze(String txt, int idx) {
740	        Pattern re = Pattern.compile("\\{\\{c" + idx + "::(.+?)\\}\\}");
741	        Matcher m = re.matcher(txt);
742	        Set<String> matches = new LinkedHashSet<>();
743	        // LinkedHashSet: make entries appear only once, like Anki desktop (see also issue #2208), and keep the order
744	        // they appear in.
745	        String groupOne;
746	        int colonColonIndex = -1;
747	        while (m.find()) {
748	            groupOne = m.group(1);
749	            colonColonIndex = groupOne.indexOf("::");
750	            if (colonColonIndex > -1) {
751	                // Cut out the hint.
752	                groupOne = groupOne.substring(0, colonColonIndex);
753	            }
754	            matches.add(groupOne);
755	        }
756	        // Now do what the pythonic ", ".join(matches) does in a tricky way
757	        String prefix = "";
758	        StringBuilder resultBuilder = new StringBuilder();
759	        for (String match : matches) {
760	            resultBuilder.append(prefix);
761	            resultBuilder.append(match);
762	            prefix = ", ";
763	        }
764	        return resultBuilder.toString();
765	    }

## Diagnosis

**File:** `AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/Previewer.java`

The `Previewer` activity declares only `android:configChanges="locale"` in the manifest, so a screen rotation **destroys and recreates** the activity (unlike `Reviewer`, which declares `orientation|screenSize` and handles rotation itself).

On recreation, `Previewer.onCreate()` re-read its entire state from the launching `Intent`:

```java
mCardList = getIntent().getLongArrayExtra("cardList");
mIndex = getIntent().getIntExtra("index", -1);
```

The `Intent` is immutable and still holds the *original* starting index from `CardBrowser`. Every navigation the user performed (`mIndex++` / `mIndex--` in `mSelectScrollHandler`) lived only in the in-memory field and was never persisted — `Previewer` overrode neither `onSaveInstanceState` nor `onRestoreInstanceState`. So rotation discarded all navigation and snapped the preview back to the card the browser originally opened.

The same applied to `mShowingAnswer`: `onCollectionLoaded()` unconditionally called `displayCardQuestion()`, so rotating while viewing an answer also flipped back to the question side.

## Fix

1. **Added `onSaveInstanceState()`** persisting `mIndex` and `mShowingAnswer`.
2. **`onCreate()` prefers the saved bundle over the Intent** when `savedInstanceState != null`, falling back to the Intent values as defaults (so a fresh launch is unchanged).
3. **`onCollectionLoaded()` restores the visible side** — it still calls `displayCardQuestion()` first (required, since that's what populates `mTypeCorrect`/`mTypeInput` and the sound list that `displayCardAnswer()` consumes), then replays `displayCardAnswer()` if the answer was showing. Capturing `restoreAnswer` into a local is necessary because `displayCardQuestion()` clears `mShowingAnswer`.
4. **Hardened the guard** with a `mCardList == null` check — previously that line would NPE if the extra were ever absent.

Since `updateButtonState()` reads `mIndex`/`mShowingAnswer`, the `<`/`>` navigation buttons and their disabled-at-the-edges states also come back correct after rotation.
